instruction: Find the first URL in the most recent Bills email and open it in a Chrome browser tab.

metadata.explanation: Variation 4: Phrasing emphasizes finding the URL then opening it. Task locates the first link (https://www.amazon.com/) in the latest Bills email and opens it in Chrome. Evaluator verifies all three tabs are open including the new amazon.com tab.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses get_open_tabs_info getter to extract all Chrome tab URLs
Metric is_expected_tabs properly compares expected tab URLs against actual tab URLs
Expected value (amazon.com) is correctly identified as the first URL in the Bills email based on task metadata
Data flow is logically sound: getter extracts tab URLs -> metric compares -> returns pass/fail
Evaluator can semantically verify that the amazon.com URL was successfully opened in Chrome
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The evaluator checks for ALL 3 tabs (apple.com, scholar.google.com, amazon.com), but the instruction only requires opening amazon.com. This is over-specified but not incorrect.

Minor: Verify that are_lists_equal uses set-based comparison rather than order-sensitive comparison. If order matters, an agent that opens amazon.com in a different tab position would incorrectly fail.

Consider: The instruction doesn't explicitly require keeping the initial 2 tabs open, so checking for exactly 3 tabs is stricter than necessary. A more lenient check would verify amazon.com is among open tabs without requiring the exact set.
